stories.title: Sports roundup: Kipchoge wants a marathon major in Kenya, Real Madrid hit PSV for five, Arsenal and City held
key_points: Eliud Kipchoge says Kenya should chase a World Marathon Major, at the launch of the new Sisibo Marathon in Eldoret.
The Sisibo Marathon on December 19 offers Ksh25 million in prizes, Ksh5 million for each winner, organisers say.
Champions League: Real Madrid beat PSV 5-1; Arsenal drew 1-1 with Dortmund; Man City drew 2-2 with Napoli.
Aston Villa lost 1-0 at Galatasaray. PSG play Roma on Wednesday.
stories.content:
Here is the top sports news of the last two days, starting at home in Kenya.

Kipchoge: Kenya should host a marathon major

Marathon great Eliud Kipchoge says Kenya should aim to host one of the World Marathon Majors, the group of the biggest city marathons such as London, Berlin and New York. He spoke on Sunday at the launch of the new Sisibo Marathon in Eldoret, The Standard reported.

Kipchoge said he hopes the Sisibo race can become Africa's first World Marathon Major in 2027. That is his hope; no official bid decision has been reported. He also called for a Diamond League athletics meeting in Kenya. Athletics Kenya president Jackson Tuwei supported bringing more global events to Kenya and also spoke about the fight against doping.

Olympic 1500m champion Faith Kipyegon and New York City Marathon champion Sheila Chepkirui were among the stars at the launch.

Sisibo Marathon: big prize money

The first Sisibo Marathon will be run in Eldoret on December 19, 2026, according to Uasin Gishu News. Athletics Kenya official Barnaba Korir announced total prize money of Ksh25 million. The men's and women's winners will each get Ksh5 million, second place Ksh3 million and third place Ksh1 million. Organisers say it will be the richest race in Kenya and Africa, and that entry will be free and open to all.

Why it matters: Big races at home give Kenyan runners a chance to earn well without travelling abroad, and can bring visitors and money to the North Rift.

Champions League: Real Madrid strong, English clubs held

Tuesday night was matchday five of the Champions League league phase. Results, from AFP and France 24 reports:

  • Real Madrid 5-1 PSV Eindhoven: PSV led at half-time through an Ivan Perisic penalty. Madrid hit back with goals from Federico Valverde, Jude Bellingham, two from Kylian Mbappe and one from Vinicius Junior. Madrid have won all five games and have 15 points.
  • Arsenal 1-1 Borussia Dortmund: Viktor Gyokeres scored early for Arsenal, but Maximilian Beier levelled after the break.
  • Manchester City 2-2 Napoli: City came from behind twice. Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang scored for Napoli; Ayyoub Bouaddi and a late Rayan Cherki goal earned City a point.
  • Galatasaray 1-0 Aston Villa: a late Deniz Gul header beat Villa, who stay on nine points.
  • Other results: Como 1-0 AEK Athens, Slovan Bratislava 0-2 Real Betis, RB Leipzig 3-1 Lens, Bodo/Glimt 1-0 LASK.

On Wednesday, Paris Saint-Germain host Roma. A PSG win would take them level with Real Madrid on 15 points.

Coming up

In the Premier League this weekend, the big game is Arsenal against Manchester City on Sunday. At home, the row between Harambee Stars coach Benni McCarthy and the Football Kenya Federation over team preparations is still being watched closely by fans.

stories.title: World roundup: Israeli strike kills Hamas security chief, Russia hits Zaporizhzhia, Amnesty raises Tigray war crimes concern
key_points: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed a senior Hamas security official and others on Tuesday, Reuters reported.
A Russian attack on an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, killed 2 people, a Ukrainian official said.
Amnesty International says Ethiopian shelling of towns in Tigray should be investigated as possible war crimes.
Bangladesh's former leader Sheikh Hasina plans to return on December 16; the government says she will be arrested.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the last day, in short and simple form. Most details come from Reuters reports, as summarised by the US website Just Security.

1. Gaza: Israeli strikes kill Hamas security chief

Israeli airstrikes on Tuesday killed Naeem Abu Nahel, described as the head of Hamas's internal security service in Gaza, and six other people, Reuters reported, citing medics and police. One strike hit western Gaza City. Others hit areas near Khan Younis and the Netzarim corridor.

The Israeli military and the Shin Bet security service said they struck a senior Hamas militant. The Hamas-run interior ministry said two of the dead were police officers. These claims have not been independently checked.

Why it matters: Each new strike puts more strain on the fragile Gaza truce and on aid for people living in tents during winter.

2. Ukraine: Russian strike hits apartment block in Zaporizhzhia

An overnight Russian attack hit an apartment building in the city of Zaporizhzhia, killing two people, Reuters reported. Regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said dozens were wounded, including children. Early reports gave different numbers for the wounded, so the final count is not yet clear.

Why it matters: The attacks go on while efforts at peace talks continue. The war still affects global food and fuel prices.

3. Ethiopia: Amnesty calls for war crimes probe in Tigray

Rights group Amnesty International said artillery strikes on towns in northern Tigray this year by Ethiopian forces and allied militia should be investigated as possible war crimes, Reuters reported. Amnesty also accused the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) of putting civilians at risk during the September battle for the town of Alamata, by placing fighters in homes and using schools. These are Amnesty's findings; Ethiopia's response was not included in the reports we saw.

Why it matters: Ethiopia is Kenya's neighbour. New fighting in Tigray could affect refugees, trade and peace in the Horn of Africa.

4. Bangladesh: Hasina says she will return on December 16

Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to go back to Bangladesh on December 16, her spokesperson told Reuters. She has lived in India since she was removed from power in 2024. A Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in her absence last year over the deadly crackdown on the 2024 protests. Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir said she would not return on her own terms and would be brought back in handcuffs, the BBC reported.

5. US: doubt over end of military aid to Israel

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, said he is not sure that about $3.8 billion a year in US military aid to Israel will end by the end of 2026, as President Donald Trump said on November 3, Reuters reported. Huckabee said the aid is meant to continue for two more years.

Why it matters: US decisions on foreign aid, from military help to health funding, affect many countries, including Kenya.

stories.title: eCitizen hack claim: what Kenyans in the US should do now to protect their accounts
key_points: Hackers claim they stole about 740GB of data from Kenya's eCitizen portal. The government has not confirmed any data loss.
The State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services says it is investigating and eCitizen still works as usual.
Users are told to change their password, use a strong one, and never share their password or OTP code.
Kenyans abroad use eCitizen for passports and other services, so this matters to the diaspora.
stories.content:
The Kenyan government is investigating claims that hackers broke into eCitizen, the website Kenyans use for most government services. It has asked users to change their passwords. For Kenyans in the United States, who use eCitizen for passports and many other services, this is a good time to check your account.

What happened

On Tuesday, November 24, the State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services said it was aware of reports of a possible hack and was investigating. This office is part of the Ministry of Interior, led by Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen.

The office said it is checking how far any damage went and whether any data reached the wrong people. It said "eCitizen services remain available" and people can keep using government services as usual. It promised updates after its technical investigation.

What the hackers claim

A group calling itself "ByteToBreach" claims it took about 740GB of data, according to Mwakilishi, which cited a cyber security monitoring firm called VECERT Analyser. The group claims this includes:

  • about 600GB of personal identity and verification documents;
  • about 100GB of government database records;
  • about 40GB of computer code.

Reports also say the attackers claim they reached systems linked to the Social Health Authority (SHA), the DCI and the National Police Service. None of these claims has been confirmed. The government has not confirmed a breach, the amount of data, or that any data was lost.

What you should do now: step by step

  • Step 1: Log in to eCitizen only by typing the official address yourself. Do not click links in texts or emails.
  • Step 2: Change your eCitizen password. Choose a long, strong password you do not use anywhere else.
  • Step 3: If you used the same password for email, banking or M-Pesa, change those passwords too.
  • Step 4: Never share your password or one-time PIN (OTP). The government says eCitizen will never ask you for them.
  • Step 5: Be careful with calls, WhatsApp messages or emails that say they are from eCitizen, the embassy or immigration. Scammers often use news like this to trick people.
  • Step 6: Check your account for anything strange, such as applications or payments you did not make, and report it through official channels.

Why this matters for the diaspora

Kenyans abroad depend on eCitizen for passport applications and renewals, ID and civil registration services, and paying government fees. Many of them upload copies of passports, IDs and birth certificates. That is why the claim of stolen identity documents worries many people abroad, even though it is not yet confirmed.

If you have a passport or other application in progress, the government says services are still running. Keep watching official government and embassy channels for updates, and avoid sharing unverified posts.

Also this week

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi Movement tour of the US continues in the Maryland and Washington DC area this week. Next is a Thanksgiving dinner in Dallas on November 27, then Houston on November 29, according to the tour schedule reported by Capital FM.

stories.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to bring back ambassadors after Ruto-Tshisekedi talks in Oyo
key_points: Ruto and DR Congo's President Tshisekedi met in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, on Sunday, November 22.
They agreed to work towards full diplomatic ties, including the return of ambassadors. No date has been given.
The two countries have had no ambassadors in each other's capitals for years, after a row over the M23-linked AFC alliance launched in Nairobi in December 2023.
At home on Tuesday, Ruto said the Hustler Fund will get Ksh5 billion more and some borrowing limits will rise.
stories.content:
Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have agreed to repair their broken relationship. President William Ruto and DRC President Felix Tshisekedi met on Sunday, November 22, in Oyo, a town in the Republic of the Congo. They agreed to work towards full diplomatic ties, including bringing back ambassadors.

Who brought them together

The talks were hosted by Republic of the Congo President Denis Sassou N'Guesso. Togo's leader, Faure Gnassingbé, who is the African Union's mediator for eastern DRC, helped lead the talks. Ruto cut short his tour of Western Kenya to travel to Oyo, Dawan Africa and Xinhua reported.

What went wrong between the two countries

The trouble started in December 2023. A new political and military alliance, the Congo River Alliance (AFC), was launched in Nairobi. The AFC is linked to the M23 rebels who fight the Congolese army in eastern DRC. Kinshasa was angry and recalled its ambassador from Kenya, according to Xinhua and Uganda's The Independent.

Relations got worse after that. In January 2025, rioters in Kinshasa attacked and looted the Kenyan embassy, Kenyans.co.ke reported. The DRC also did not accept Kenya's chosen ambassador, Peter Tum. In October 2025, Nairobi hosted Congolese opposition figures, including former president Joseph Kabila. Kenya said it could not stop people from expressing political views.

What they agreed

According to a joint statement reported by several outlets, the two leaders agreed to:

  • work towards full diplomatic relations, including the return of ambassadors;
  • restart their Joint Grand Commission for Cooperation and hold regular talks;
  • solve differences through dialogue and respect each other's borders and independence;
  • grow trade, investment and security cooperation;
  • work together on stopping Ebola.

Ruto said the two countries had agreed to "open a new chapter", Dawan Africa reported. The DRC presidency said on X that the leaders agreed to fully restore relations, notably through the return of their ambassadors, according to Xinhua.

Outlets used slightly different words. Citizen Digital said the leaders agreed to "work towards" restoring ambassadors, while Xinhua said they agreed to "fully restore" ties. No outlet has reported a date for the ambassadors to return. Kenya's foreign ministry has not given further details in the reports we saw.

Why it matters

The DRC is a big trade partner for Kenya and a member of the East African Community (EAC). Many Kenyan traders, truck drivers and businesses work in eastern DRC. Better ties could make trade and travel easier. The two countries also share the fight against Ebola in the region.

Also in Kenya politics on Tuesday

Hustler Fund: Speaking at State House, Nairobi, at a Joyful Women Organisation (JOYWO) event, Ruto said the government will add Ksh5 billion to the Hustler Fund. He said more than 4.5 million borrowers will move to a bridge loan of up to Ksh150,000, and those stuck at a Ksh10,000 limit will get higher limits if they repay, Kenyans.co.ke reported.

Malala stays with DCP: Cleophas Malala, deputy leader of Rigathi Gachagua's DCP party, denied reports that he has joined Senator Edwin Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi Movement or is running for Nairobi governor. He said he is still running for Kakamega governor on a DCP ticket, according to Kenyans.co.ke.

stories.title: Sports roundup: FKF hits back at McCarthy, Brentford thrash Everton, US and UK to host Women's World Cups
key_points: FKF says it never picks the Harambee Stars squad and that McCarthy's November pay was made early.
Brentford beat Everton 4-0 on Monday night to close the Premier League round.
FIFA gave the 2031 Women's World Cup to the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, and 2035 to the UK, Anadolu reported.
Big game on Sunday: Arsenal v Manchester City.
stories.content:
Here is the latest sports news, starting at home.

Harambee Stars: FKF and McCarthy row grows

The Football Kenya Federation (FKF) has rejected claims that its officials interfere in choosing the Harambee Stars squad, Dawan Africa reported. FKF Head of Communications Jeff Kinyanjui said on X that only the coach and his technical staff pick the players.

The row started after Kenya lost 2-1 to South Africa at Nyayo Stadium on November 17 in an AFCON qualifier. Coach Benni McCarthy then complained about hotels, meals, transport and late payments to players, The Star reported. He said the players came close to a strike before they were paid.

Kinyanjui said on local radio that McCarthy was trying to shift attention from his comments after the match. He said McCarthy's November salary was paid in advance, and that the government, not FKF, pays the coach. Dawan Africa noted that in March 2025, FKF President Hussein Mohamed said the federation would pay McCarthy, according to K24 Digital.

McCarthy apologised on November 19 for his reaction to online criticism after the loss. Kenya is third in its group with two points from four games. The team is already in AFCON 2027 as a co-host with Uganda and Tanzania, and FIFA ranks Kenya 115th in the world, Kenya Today reported.

Premier League: Brentford 4-0 Everton

Brentford beat Everton 4-0 at home on Monday night to finish the weekend's games.

The weekend's other results were:

  • Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United
  • Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal
  • Chelsea 1-4 Leeds
  • Manchester City 1-1 Fulham
  • Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich
  • Coventry 3-2 Crystal Palace
  • Bournemouth 2-0 Nottingham Forest
  • Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland
  • Hull 2-0 Brighton

Coming up: Nottingham Forest v Chelsea on Friday, November 27, and Arsenal v Manchester City on Sunday, November 29.

Women's World Cup hosts chosen

FIFA has given the 2031 Women's World Cup to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. It gave the 2035 tournament to the United Kingdom, Anadolu Agency reported. Both bids had no rivals, and the vote was held at an online FIFA meeting.

The 2031 tournament will be the first with 48 teams, up from 32, and will have 104 matches. ESPN reported that Jamaica's matches will be the first senior World Cup games played in the Caribbean.

Why it matters: more teams means more places for African women's teams, including Kenya's Harambee Starlets.

Also in sport

  • Spain's LaLiga said a cyberattack between November 14 and 16 exposed personal details of fans registered on its digital services. It says the attack has been stopped.

stories.title: World roundup: Iran says 3 tankers hit mines in Hormuz, Gaza strike kills 3, Russia and Ukraine clash at the UN
key_points: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says mines set three oil tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz; this is not independently confirmed.
An Israeli drone strike killed three Palestinians at a police post in Khan Younis, a Gaza hospital source said.
Russia ruled out reviving a Black Sea grain deal at the UN; the EU announced new sanctions on Russia.
Nvidia brought back Jensen Huang as CEO.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the last day, in short and simple form.

1. Iran says three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said late on Monday that three oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, Anadolu Agency reported. The IRGC also said US air cover did not stop the incidents, and warned ships not to use what it calls "unauthorized routes."

These are Iran's claims and have not been independently confirmed. Iran closed the strait in July after US strikes resumed, and it has reported similar tanker fires several times since October, Al Jazeera and other outlets reported.

Why it matters for Kenya: a large share of the world's oil passes through this strait. Trouble there can push up fuel prices, including in Kenya.

2. Gaza: drone strike and winter floods

An Israeli drone strike killed three Palestinians and wounded five at a police post in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, early on Tuesday, a medical source at Nasser Hospital said, according to Anadolu. Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,675 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began on October 10, 2025.

US Senator Brian Schatz has asked Israel to let in winter supplies and building materials after heavy rain flooded more than 70,000 tents. Israel's aid agency, COGAT, has said it delivered tens of thousands of tents before the storms, Latin Times reported.

3. Russia and Ukraine clash at the UN

At the UN Security Council on Monday, Russia ruled out bringing back a Black Sea grain deal. It accused Ukraine of attacking more than 200 commercial ships since July, Anadolu reported. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned of new Russian strikes and asked allies for more Patriot air-defence missiles.

The President of the European Commission announced a new package of sanctions on Russia. It targets banks and crypto platforms and Russia's role in European sports and cultural events.

Why it matters for Africa: the Black Sea is a major route for wheat and fertiliser bought by African countries.

4. Nvidia brings back its CEO

Nvidia, the world's leading maker of AI chips, has reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive. The company said talks with senior US officials led its board to decide his return poses no national security risk, Anadolu reported.

5. Also today

  • South Korea sent fighter jets after Russian military planes entered its air defence zone, Yonhap reported.
  • Libya's leaders warned that the country risks being dragged into the Russia–Ukraine and Sudan conflicts.
  • Zambia and Türkiye agreed to work together on water projects, investment and climate resilience.

stories.title: Sifuna's US tour moves to Maryland and DC after packed Allentown town hall
key_points: The Allentown, Pennsylvania town hall on Sunday was filled to capacity, Mwakilishi and K24 reported.
Sifuna opened the movement's first overseas office in Hackettstown, New Jersey.
Today (Nov 24) he has a policy meeting and a luncheon with Maryland elected officials; Wednesday ends with a town hall.
Next stops: Dallas and Houston, then Seattle and California, ending December 7.
stories.content:
WASHINGTON, DC — Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's tour of the United States has reached Maryland and the Washington DC area, after a busy first weekend in New Jersey and Pennsylvania.

Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) and wants to run for president in Kenya's August 2027 election. His trip runs from November 21 to December 7, according to Mwakilishi, a news site for Kenyans in the US.

What happened at the weekend

In our Sunday story, we promised to report what happened at the Allentown town hall. Here it is.

  • New Jersey: supporters met him at Newark airport with songs, dances and banners. He opened the movement's first office outside Kenya, in Hackettstown, New Jersey. Mwakilishi said the office will run volunteer work, voter outreach and fundraising on the East Coast.
  • Pennsylvania: on Sunday, November 22, he went to a morning service at Grace Community Church in Allentown. In the afternoon, he spoke at a town hall at The Palace Center. Mwakilishi said the hall was full, with Kenyans from Pennsylvania, New York and New Jersey. K24 Digital said a video Sifuna shared showed every seat taken.

At the town hall, Sifuna answered critics who had doubted his support in the region. He talked about governance, economic accountability and the constitution, Mwakilishi reported.

This week in Maryland and DC

  • Monday, Nov 23: business community dinner in Maryland.
  • Today, Tuesday, Nov 24: an East Africa politics and policy meeting, then a luncheon with Afri Thrive and Maryland elected officials.
  • Wednesday, Nov 25: a brunch with women from the DC area, a talk with the 6.25 Movement and Gen Z Movement, and an evening town hall.

The rest of the tour

  • Texas: Thanksgiving dinner with families in Dallas on November 27; women's meeting and town hall in Houston on November 29.
  • Washington State: December 3–4, church service in Federal Way and a gala dinner in Renton.
  • California: December 5, town hall in San Francisco and a gala in Oakland; December 7, closing dinner with Kenyan professionals in Silicon Valley.

Dates and venues can change, so check with local organisers before you travel.

Why it matters

Kenyans abroad send home billions of shillings every year. But very few vote: fewer than 600 Kenyans living in the US were registered to vote in 2022, Mwakilishi reported. Analysts say tours like this one matter mostly for raising campaign money and shaping debate at home.

Back in Kenya, the opposition is asking the electoral commission to allow electronic voting for Kenyans abroad. That could change how much the diaspora vote counts in the future.

Other leaders, including Rigathi Gachagua and David Maraga, have made similar trips to the US. The Nation noted that these tours include a large fundraising part.

stories.title: IEBC's Smartmatic deal ends today as opposition sets January deadline and 94 parties are told to fix nomination rules
key_points: The IEBC's 2021 support contract with Smartmatic, its election technology supplier, ends today, November 24.
Gachagua has given the IEBC until January to answer opposition demands, or face nationwide protests.
The IEBC says court cases have slowed its buying of new election technology.
Only 11 of 105 parties passed the IEBC's first check of nomination rules; 94, including UDA and ODM, must fix theirs.
stories.content:
NAIROBI — Kenya's election body, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), reaches an important date today, Tuesday, November 24. Its support contract with Smartmatic, the company that supplies its election technology, ends today, according to People Daily and the Nation.

Smartmatic's equipment and systems were used in the 2022 General Election. The next General Election is on August 10, 2027.

Why the date matters

The IEBC uses this technology to register voters and identify them. People Daily said the end of the contract raises questions about technical support, software licences and security updates.

Opposition leader Rigathi Gachagua, the former Deputy President who now leads the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), has warned that a new system could take five to six months to buy. He says this could disrupt voter registration, Capital FM reported.

The IEBC has not said publicly what will happen after today. The Nation reported that the High Court has certified as urgent a case that seeks to stop the IEBC from giving a Sh17.6 billion election technology tender for 2027 to Smartmatic.

What the IEBC says

At a meeting with political parties on Thursday, November 19, IEBC Commissioner Anne Nderitu said court cases had slowed the buying of election technology and ballot papers, even though tenders had already been advertised, Dawan Africa reported. She said every constituency has at least four registration kits, and that the commission has the time and skills to run a credible election.

Opposition walkout and January deadline

At that same meeting, Gachagua, Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka and Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna led opposition leaders out of the room. They said the agenda left out their main concerns, Capital FM and The Standard reported.

Their main demands are:

  • clean the voter register by removing dead and ineligible voters;
  • make constituency results for president final, and end the national tallying centre at Bomas of Kenya;
  • allow electronic voting for Kenyans living abroad;
  • livestream voting, counting and the announcement of results.

Speaking at a church in Runyenjes, Embu County, on Sunday, Gachagua gave the IEBC until January to respond. He warned of nationwide protests if it does not, Dawan Africa reported. He also asked the IEBC to say when it will audit the voter register.

The government side

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen accused the opposition of resisting open tallying of presidential votes. He said the final count must happen at the national tallying centre with candidates' agents present, Capital FM reported. Senate Speaker Moses Wetang'ula urged the IEBC not to be intimidated by political groups.

94 parties must fix their nomination rules

In a separate step, the IEBC said on Friday, November 20, that it had checked the nomination rules of 105 parties. Only 11 passed. The other 94 must make changes, Citizen Digital and Capital FM reported.

The parties that passed include Wiper, Jubilee, Safina and Babu Owino's The Mwananchi Party. Those that must make changes include UDA, ODM, KANU and the Democratic Party, according to Citizen Digital. Kenya Today reported that Gachagua's DCP is also on that list.

The IEBC said parties that failed are not blocked from the 2027 election. Each party has been told what to fix and given a deadline.

What to watch: how the IEBC keeps voter registration running after today, and when the court rules on the technology tender.

stories.title: Sports roundup: CAF makes Kiswahili an official language, Liverpool thrash 10-man Man United
key_points: CAF voted in Abuja to make Kiswahili its fifth official language, ahead of AFCON 2027 in East Africa.
Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as United boss.
Harambee Stars coach Benni McCarthy complained about poor hotel and meals in South Africa.
Brentford v Everton closes the Premier League round on Monday night (8pm UK time).
stories.content:
Here is the weekend's sports news, with a big win for East Africa at the top.

Kiswahili becomes an official language of African football

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has made Kiswahili one of its official languages. The vote happened at CAF's 48th Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday, November 21, with all 54 member countries represented, KBC and P.M. News reported.

Kiswahili now joins English, French, Arabic and Portuguese. CAF said the move shows respect for Africa's many languages.

Why it matters: Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda will co-host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON). Kiswahili is spoken by more than 200 million people across East, Central and Southern Africa, according to HapaKenya.

At the same meeting, CAF reported a profit of $31.2 million on revenue of about $284 million for its 2026 financial year, and backed FIFA President Gianni Infantino for re-election, Freedom Online reported.

Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United manager ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield on Sunday.

  • United defender Leny Yoro was sent off after 8 minutes.
  • Dominik Szoboszlai (10') and Florian Wirtz (13') scored quickly for Liverpool.
  • Teenager Rio Ngumoha (66') and substitute Victor Munoz (82') added two more.

The loss keeps United in the relegation zone, one point above the bottom, Sky Sports reported.

Other Premier League results this weekend

  • Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal
  • Chelsea 1-4 Leeds
  • Manchester City 1-1 Fulham
  • Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich
  • Bournemouth 2-0 Nottingham Forest
  • Coventry 3-2 Crystal Palace
  • Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland
  • Hull 2-0 Brighton

Brentford host Everton on Monday night to close the round.

Harambee Stars: coach speaks out

Kenya's national team lost 2-1 to South Africa at Nyayo Stadium in Nairobi on November 17 in an AFCON qualifier, The Star reported. Relebohile Mofokeng scored twice for South Africa and Mohamed Bajaber got a late goal for Kenya.

Coach Benni McCarthy later said the team's hotel and meals during the trip to Johannesburg were below standard, and that the squad could not even fly home together, the Nation reported. Kenya has already qualified for AFCON 2027 as a co-host.

stories.title: World roundup: COP31 ends without a deal, Iran tensions stay high, Russia steps up attacks on Ukraine
key_points: UN climate talks in Turkey ended Sunday with no main agreement; COP32 goes to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
Fighting between the US and Iran has returned; Trump says he wants a lasting deal.
Zelenskyy asked the US to release Patriot missiles after a week of heavy Russian attacks.
UN peacekeepers in Lebanon are handing their work to the Lebanese army before their mission ends.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the weekend, in short and simple form.

1. Climate talks end with no main deal

The UN climate summit, COP31, ended in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday, November 22, without the main agreement countries were working on, UN News reported. Talks ran two days past the deadline, making it the longest UN climate summit on record.

The big fight was over coal, oil and gas. Countries hit hard by climate change wanted a clear plan to move away from fossil fuels. Big fuel exporters, such as Saudi Arabia and Russia, pushed back, CBS News and other outlets reported. The European Union, Panama and the Marshall Islands rejected the final text.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the result a deep disappointment. Ghana, speaking for the African Group, said the text fell short on money for poorer countries but did not block it.

Why it matters for Africa: the next summit, COP32, will be held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and will take up the unfinished issues.

2. US–Iran: fighting is back, talk of a deal continues

The US–Iran conflict began on February 28, 2026. A ceasefire and a June agreement followed, but that agreement broke down and fighting returned, Gulf News reported. The two sides exchanged fire again on November 17.

President Donald Trump said the US is talking to Iran and wants a deal that lasts even after he leaves office. He has not shared a plan or a timetable. Meanwhile, Anadolu Agency reported that Bahrain renewed its threat alert, after Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they had destroyed two US radar systems there. That claim has not been independently confirmed.

3. Ukraine asks for more air defence

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged the United States to approve the delivery of Patriot missiles, which can shoot down ballistic missiles, Al Jazeera reported. He said partners have already paid for them.

Zelenskyy said Russia fired about 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 guided bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine in one week. On Sunday, a Russian drone attack partly brought down an apartment building in Dymer, near Kyiv, and rescuers were searching for missing people, including children.

4. UN peacekeepers prepare to leave Lebanon

The UN force in southern Lebanon, UNIFIL, has begun handing its duties to the Lebanese army, according to Anadolu Agency. The UN Security Council voted in 2025 to end the mission on December 31, 2026, with troops leaving during 2027. Lebanese leaders have asked for more time, so far without success, the Associated Press reported.

KASS-mtv will keep you updated on these stories.

stories.title: Sifuna's US tour reaches Pennsylvania as Kenyan politicians chase diaspora money and support
key_points: Sifuna landed at Newark, New Jersey, to a lively welcome from Kenyans waving flags.
Sunday's plan: church at Grace Community Church, then a town hall at The Palace Center, Allentown.
Next stops: Maryland and the Washington DC area from Nov 23.
Analysts say US tours are mostly about raising campaign money.
stories.content:
ALLENTOWN, Pennsylvania — Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's tour of the United States moved to Pennsylvania on Sunday, November 22, the second day of a 17-day trip to meet Kenyans living in America.

Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) and has said he will run for president in Kenya's August 2027 election.

A warm welcome

Sifuna landed at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, where dozens of Kenyans waved flags and chanted as his team arrived, Uzalendo News reported. The Star said supporters broke into song and dance when they saw him.

He is travelling with Vihiga Senator Godfrey Osotsi and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, according to The Star.

The tour's plan was to open an LMM office in Hackettstown, New Jersey, at noon on Saturday, November 21.

Sunday in Allentown

The published programme for Sunday was:

  • a morning church service at Grace Community Church in Allentown;
  • a town hall meeting at The Palace Center, from 2pm to 6pm.

KASS-mtv had not yet seen reports of what was said at the town hall when this story was written. We will update readers when we do.

Where the tour goes next

  • Nov 23–25: Maryland and the Washington DC area — community dinner, policy meeting, women's brunch, Gen Z meeting and a town hall;
  • Late November: Dallas and Houston, Texas;
  • Early December: Seattle and California, ending on December 7.

Dates have changed before, so check with the organisers before you travel.

Why politicians keep coming to the US

Sifuna is not the first. Democracy for the Citizens Party leader Rigathi Gachagua made a long US tour earlier this year, with stops that included Oregon, Kansas, Dallas, Boston and Spokane, the Nation reported. The Star reported that Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka is also planning a US tour.

Analysts say money is a big reason. Political analyst Martin Andati told The Star the tours are mainly about fundraising, because the number of Kenyans living abroad is small compared with voters at home. Prof Kefa Otiso of Bowling Green State University told the Nation that the diaspora also helps politicians by persuading family and friends back home.

The money Kenyans in the US send home

Kenyans in the US are the country's biggest source of money sent home, but that flow has slowed this year. Central Bank of Kenya Governor Kamau Thugge said total remittances fell 1.3% in the 12 months to August 2026, mostly because less money came from the US and Saudi Arabia, Kenyans.co.ke reported. Kenyans.co.ke has also linked part of the slowdown to a new US tax on money transfers.

According to The Rio Times, citing CBK figures, money from the US in October 2026 was about US$178 million, 28% lower than a year earlier.

For Kenyans in America, that makes the coming town halls a chance to ask candidates direct questions about jobs, remittance costs and how the diaspora can vote.

stories.title: Opposition leaders reject 'third force' talk as Gachagua promises Mt Kenya direction before Christmas
key_points: Matiang'i, Nyoro and Karua told a Kirinyaga church on Sunday that the opposition is one team.
They said the opposition will field one presidential candidate, but gave no date or method.
In Embu, Gachagua said he will give Mt Kenya its political direction before Christmas.
Gachagua also asked the IEBC to say when the voter register will be audited.
stories.content:
NAIROBI — Three opposition leaders used a church service in Kirinyaga on Sunday, November 22, to deny reports that they are building a separate "third force" inside the opposition.

At the same time, in neighbouring Embu County, former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua held his own church meeting and set out his plans for the Mt Kenya vote.

What happened in Kirinyaga

Jubilee Party leader Fred Matiang'i, People's Party of Kenya (PPK) leader Ndindi Nyoro and People's Liberation Party (PLP) leader Martha Karua attended a service at Kimunye ACK Church, The Star reported. Kirinyaga is Ms Karua's home county. MPs Anthony Kibagendi (Kitutu South), Clive Gisairo (Kitutu Masaba) and Patrick Osero (Borabu) were also there.

The four leaders, together with Siaya Governor James Orengo, have toured several regions together in recent weeks, including Gusii. The Nation reported that this had fuelled talk of a new power bloc that could shape who the opposition picks as its presidential candidate.

The leaders said that is not true:

  • Nyoro said, according to The Star: "There is only one force in the Opposition." He said the opposition will pick one flagbearer, and that leaders missing from Kirinyaga were meeting supporters in Embu and other places.
  • Matiang'i said the opposition has no time for fighting and accused unnamed people of trying to divide it for their own gain. "We have one team in Kenya in the opposition," he said, as quoted by The Kenya Times.
  • Karua said the leaders' different tours are planned together to win support across the country, and that the opposition will settle on one candidate to face President William Ruto.

According to The Kenya Times, Ms Karua has also said she is ready to step aside and back either Matiang'i or Nyoro if the opposition chooses one of them. The opposition has not yet said how or when it will pick its candidate.

What Gachagua said in Embu

Mr Gachagua, who leads the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), spoke at Wonders of God Church in Karurumo, Runyenjes, People Daily reported. He said:

  • he will give the Mt Kenya region its political direction before Christmas, after months of meetings with residents. The Kenya Times reported the dates as December 22 or 23;
  • families can use the holidays to discuss and agree on the region's preferred candidates;
  • the IEBC should say when it will audit the voter register, and remove dead voters and foreigners he claims are on it. People Daily noted he did not give evidence for the claim about foreigners.

Citizen Digital reported that Mr Gachagua also said opposition leaders now hold key voting regions, naming Mt Kenya for himself, Kisii for Matiang'i and Lower Eastern for Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka.

Why it matters

Kenya's next general election is in August 2027. The opposition has many leaders who want to run for president, and every one of them says the group will back a single candidate. How they choose that person is the big question for the coming months.

The IEBC had not publicly responded to Mr Gachagua's demands by the time of writing.

stories.title: Sifuna brings Linda Mwananchi tour to Kenyans in the US, starting Saturday in New Jersey
key_points: The tour starts Saturday, Nov 21, in Hackettstown, New Jersey, and ends Dec 7 in Silicon Valley, California.
Stops include Pennsylvania, Maryland, Washington DC, Texas, Seattle and California.
Plans include town halls, community dinners and meetings with Gen Z groups.
The dates have changed before, so check with the organisers before you travel.
stories.content:
Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna is taking his Linda Mwananchi Movement to Kenyans in the United States, with a tour that starts this Saturday in New Jersey.

The movement says the tour will open on November 21 with a new Linda Mwananchi office in Hackettstown, New Jersey, at noon, and end in Silicon Valley, California, on December 7.

Where and when (latest published plan)

  • Nov 21, Hackettstown, NJ: office opening at noon
  • Nov 22, Allentown, PA: church service, then a town hall at Palace Center from 2pm to 6pm
  • Nov 23, Maryland: community dinner at Spark Hotel at 7:30pm
  • Nov 24, Washington, DC
  • Nov 27, Dallas, TX
  • Nov 29, Houston, TX
  • Dec 3–4, Seattle area, WA: Renton and Federal Way
  • Dec 5, San Francisco and Oakland, CA
  • Dec 7, Silicon Valley, CA

The plan includes town hall meetings, community dinners, sessions with Gen Z groups and meetings with elected officials, Capital FM reported.

Earlier versions of the schedule were different. A programme reported by the Nation and The Standard in early November had Sifuna arriving in Allentown on November 20 and finishing in Seattle and California by December 4. Please confirm times and venues with the organisers before travelling.

Why the tour matters

Sifuna is seen as a rising challenger to President William Ruto ahead of the August 2027 election. The Nation reported that the trip aims to win over diaspora voters and raise money for his campaign.

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua made a similar US trip from August 26 to October 9, with stops including Spokane, Portland, Kansas, Dallas and Boston.

The visit also comes as the money Kenyans abroad send home is slowing down:

  • October: Central Bank of Kenya figures show remittances were $430.5 million in October 2026, down 1.9% from October 2025.
  • 12 months to October: remittances fell 1.1% to $5.023 billion.
  • From the US: money from Kenya's biggest source fell 12.6% in the first half of the year, according to Business Daily. A new US tax on money transfers began on January 1.

stories.title: Ruto starts 8-day Western Kenya tour as poll shows Sifuna ahead in the region
key_points: Ruto is touring all four Western counties: Busia, Kakamega, Vihiga and Bungoma.
A Tifa poll last week put Senator Edwin Sifuna at 55% in Western, against Ruto's 25%.
Ruto launched roads, markets, a cultural centre and electricity connections.
Kenya's next general election is in August 2027.
stories.content:
NAIROBI — President William Ruto has begun an eight-day campaign tour of Western Kenya, a region where a new poll shows Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna well ahead of him.

The tour covers all four Western counties — Busia, Kakamega, Vihiga and Bungoma — and is split into two parts, with rest days in between, The Star reported on Friday.

On Thursday, Ruto was in Busia and Bungoma. In Teso North, Busia, he:

  • opened the Kakapel Cultural Centre;
  • opened new classrooms and offices at Kapkemer Comprehensive Primary School;
  • launched work on the Butula–Nambale–Amukura–Machakusi–Kocholia road;
  • started the Last Mile electricity connection project at Segero Centre.

In Bungoma, he launched two road projects, laid the foundation stone for Bokoli Modern Market and opened Naitiri Modern Market in Tongaren.

On Friday he was due in Budalang'i and Funyula in Busia, then Butere and Shinyalu in Kakamega. Saturday's plan includes Matungu, Sirisia and Vihiga.

Why Western matters now

The trip comes a week after a Tifa poll found 55% support for Sifuna in Western, against 25% for Ruto. Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement and is seen as a growing challenger ahead of the 2027 election.

Western has long voted with the late Raila Odinga. Ruto had been expected to win much of that support through his working deal with ODM, but Sifuna's rise has changed the picture. Ruto also needs Western votes to make up for support he may lose in Mt Kenya after his split with former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua.

Speaking in Teso North, Ruto accused his rivals of dividing people along tribal lines and said they have no plans for schools, electricity, roads or health. "Those people, we shall show them dust in the elections," he said.

Several leaders joined him:

  • Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi;
  • National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula;
  • Cooperatives Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya;
  • Busia Governor Paul Otuoma.

Oparanya said ODM remains in the broad-based government and will back Ruto's re-election. Wetang'ula urged a big turnout in August next year.

According to The Star, Ruto has visited about 24 counties in the past two months.

KASS-mtv will follow the rest of the tour.
